blocks.content:
### Trimming

Pick **Trim Entities**, choose **Power Trim**, then click and drag your cursor across the piece of line you want gone. It disappears where it crosses another line. This is how you turn overlapping shapes into one clean outline.

If trim takes more than it should, press **Ctrl+Z** and drag a shorter stroke.

### Dragging

Any endpoint can be dragged. Click it and move it. This is faster than deleting and redrawing.

Sketch geometry is colored on purpose:

- **Blue** means under-defined. It can still be dragged. This is fine for today.
- **Black** means fully defined. It will not move.
- **Red** means over-defined. Something conflicts. Undo the last thing you added.

### Relations

SolidWorks adds relations automatically while you draw. The small yellow icons that appear near your cursor are it telling you what it is about to lock in.

| Icon meaning | What it forces |
|---|---|
| Coincident | Two points sit on top of each other |
| Horizontal / Vertical | A line stays flat or straight up |
| Tangent | An arc meets a line smoothly, no corner |
| Equal | Two lines or circles stay the same size |

To add one yourself, select two entities, then pick the relation from the panel on the left.

To delete one, click the small green icon in the sketch and press **Delete**.

sections.blurb: What to do when you are stuck and Mr. Pina is across the room.
sections.title: Getting Unstuck

blocks.content:
### Screenshot it and ask

SolidWorks and xTool Studio have hundreds of buttons. Describing the one you are looking at is slow. Showing it is fast.

1. Press **Win + Shift + S**. The screen dims and your cursor becomes a crosshair.
2. Drag a box around the part you are stuck on. Include the whole dialog or the whole toolbar, not just the button.
3. The image is now on your clipboard.
4. Open an AI chat, press **Ctrl + V**, and type your question.

Give it the context or it will guess. Something like: *I am in SolidWorks making a dogtag outline for class. This is my sketch. Why will it not let me trim this line?*

blocks.title: This is allowed, and it is the point
blocks.content:
This assignment is AI level 1, COACH. Use it any time you are stuck, not only after you have tried everything. It can explain a tool, walk you through a menu, or tell you why something is not working.

What it does not do is make the tag. The shape, the hole, what goes on it, and which process each feature gets are yours.

rows.ask: How do I close a gap between two endpoints in a SolidWorks sketch?
What does this option in the DXF export wizard do?
rows.not: What settings should I pick? Just tell me.

rows.ask: Why is my sketch line red instead of black?
What is the difference between score and engrave on a laser?
rows.not: Which one should I use for everything?

blocks.title: Questions that work, and questions that do not
Two rules that never change
blocks.content:
**Verify it.** AI is confident when it is wrong. If it names a menu that is not there, it made it up. Check against the actual program.

**Explain it.** You can be asked to explain any part of what you submitted, in your own words, at any time. Work you cannot explain gets corrected before it earns credit.

sections.blurb: The single thing that makes or breaks a laser file.
sections.title: Closed Loops

blocks.title: A gap you cannot see will still fail
blocks.content: The laser needs to know what is inside your shape and what is outside. A loop with a gap anywhere has no inside, so the machine cannot cut it. A gap of one thousandth of an inch fails exactly the same as an obvious one.

### Finding a gap

Drag the whole sketch by one line. Everything connected moves together. Anything that stays behind was never attached.

### Closing a gap

Drag one endpoint onto the other and hold until the **coincident** icon appears next to your cursor, then release. The two points are now one point.

### Stray entities

Anything left over inside your outline is a line the machine will try to follow. Construction lines you added and forgot, a circle you drew twice, half of a shape you trimmed. Delete them before you exit the sketch.

sections.blurb: How the geometry gets from SolidWorks to the laser, and what usually goes wrong.
sections.title: DXF Export

blocks.content:
### The order matters

Select the **flat face** of the extruded tag first, then **File, Save As, DXF**. The export wizard reads the face you already selected. If you start the export with nothing selected, the wizard asks you to pick, and it is easy to pick the wrong one.

### Check it before you leave

When the DXF opens in xTool Studio, you should see exactly two shapes: your outline and your hole. Anything else means something came along that should not have.

rows.fix: Re-export with the part set to inches, or scale it in xTool Studio and note it
rows.cause: Units mismatch between the part and the export

rows.fix: Re-export with only the flat face selected
rows.cause: The side wall of the extrude exported along with the face
rows.symptom: Extra outline just outside the first

rows.fix: Go back to the sketch and close the circle
rows.cause: The circle was not closed, so it was not a hole

rows.fix: Save As again and confirm the type is DXF
rows.cause: Saved as DWG or the wizard was cancelled

sections.title: Cut, Score, Engrave

rows.use: The outline and the chain hole. Nothing else.
rows.does: Burns all the way through the metal

rows.use: Borders, outlines of shapes, thin line art
rows.does: Follows a line and marks it without going through
Sweeps back and forth and darkens an area

blocks.title: Cut is the one that ends the part
blocks.content: Anything assigned cut becomes a hole. If you assign cut to your name, your name falls out of the tag and what is left is a stencil. Check every feature in the preview before you finish.

sections.blurb: What to bring in, and what will come out as a gray smudge.
sections.title: Images That Engrave Well

blocks.content:
### The rule

The laser has two settings for any spot: marked or not marked. It has no gray. Anything that depends on shading to be recognizable will not survive.

High contrast, hard edges, and large shapes work. Detail smaller than about the width of a pencil line disappears.

rows.why: Imports as real vectors, so it can be scored or cut as well as engraved, and it scales without going fuzzy
Hard edges, no shading to lose. Use a transparent or plain white background
Works if the strokes are thick. Thin outlines vanish
Everything recognizable in a photo is shading, and shading is what the laser cannot do
Comes out as blotches with a hard edge where the machine picked a side
Small text turns into a solid dark bar. Use the text tool instead

blocks.title: What you are allowed to put on it
blocks.content: School appropriate, and yours to use. No copyrighted characters, no team or company logos you do not own, nothing you would not hand to the Dean. You are taking this tag home and wearing it.
